135663.overview: Due to an engine malfunction, your spaceship crashes on the planet Targ. Unlike your trusty vessel, you survive the crash and now have to find a way to get away from this planet. But hey, while you're at it, you might as well try to get some money off your unplanned stay on Targ. You're a mercenary, and it just so happens that the two races on the planet are at war. So why not use that to your advantage and do some favors for each race... against cash? You play this game in a first-person perspective with vector graphics. There's a huge planet for you to explore, you can walk around on it or take airborne vehicles to reach elevated locations.

164177.overview: Mac must neutralize 18 single-screen vaults in this early platformer. He can climb ladders and safely fall any distance, as long as he lands on smooth ground. The puzzle aspect of the gameplay involves switches, which can remove walls, create floors and freeze obstacles. They must be pushed in the right order to allow access to parts of the room which contain other switches. A lack of air creates a time limit, with bonus points awarded for however much air is left when the screen is completed.

164178.overview: In a land of dinosaurs and hardships, humans have to be tough to survive, but unfortunately a new breed of human has started appearing, 'The Wimp'. Unable to hunt, these men need a special vitamin to keep them alive, but these are in dangerous places with many hazards. You play one wimp, Mr. Puniverse as you attempt to collect vitamins in this flick-screen platform game. One or two players take it in turns after a loss of life trying not to let your energy bar decrease fully, or you lose one of eight lives, and you lose a life if you fall from a height. There are objects that fire at you and pillars that move up and down, and if these are touched then a life is also lost.

164254.overview: Myriad is a side view single screen shooter where you control a spacecraft at the bottom of the screen, moving in four directions, blasting various waves of aliens that appear at the top of the screen. As you blast the aliens, they move around the screen dropping bombs on you and if you hit an alien or its bomb then you lose one of five lives. Your ship is also equipped with a limited amount of shields which protects you for a short time. There is a two player option (not on the VIC-20) and each player takes it in turns to play when the other player is killed.

165051.overview:
A compilation of Paul Woakes's 3D exploration and flight game Mercenary, and the Second City expansion pack. For some systems this was a compilation of previously-released titles, for others it was the only release for either part of the gameworld.
 
Due to an engine malfunction, your spaceship crashes on the planet Targ. Unlike your trusty vessel, you survive the crash and now have to find a way to get away from this planet. But hey, while you're at it, you might as well try to get some money off your unplanned stay on Targ.

You're a mercenary, and it just so happens that the two races on the planet are at war. So why not use that to your advantage and do some favors for each race... against cash?

You play this game in a first-person perspective with vector graphics. There's a huge planet for you to explore, you can walk around on it or take airborne vehicles to reach elevated locations.

Mercenary: The Second City is an expansion disk for Mercenary, which features the same gameplay and controls.

Following the successes over Targ's Central City, the controller of the BENSON computer relaxes and enjoys himself. Soon however, he grows bored and starts looking around for new challenges on the still hazardous Planet Targ. Rumors about the Palyar Commander's brother-in-law living in the southern hemisphere suggest that this may be a good challenge. In this Second City, the battle between Palyars and Mechanoids still rages... and nothing is as it seems.

169622.overview:
Inspired by the arcade game Centipede, a garden is in the height of summer but is full of unsavory creatures and a mutant mushroom monster called Minipede. You must blast the Minipede to clear a level as well as the other creatures including spiders, snails and ladybirds for bonus points over 15 levels. You sit at the bottom of the screen where you can move left or right, and forwards a short distance as well as backwards. The Minipede moves across the screen from the top and advances downwards when it reaches one side of the screen. Scattered around the screen in many numbers are mushrooms which can hinder your movements and when the Minipede hits one it changes direction. If you touch any creature then you lose one of four lives.

The C64 version has 14 different creatures while the C16\Plus4 and VIC 20 have 10.

186613.overview:
Monty Mole was imprisoned due to his coal theft in Wanted: Monty Mole, and rescued by Sam Stoat in Monty is Innocent. Now he has to get out of Britain while he still can.

Like the original, the game is a flick-screen platformer with puzzly leanings. Learning the movement paths of enemies, and the timing sequence of the crushers, and working out a path across the screen by using the offered ropes and platforms. Not all parts of all screens can be accessed at once.

You will need to collect money and other items along the way. Before starting the game, you must choose five items from a selection of 21 to form your 'Freedom Kit' – correct selections are essential to complete the game, and a degree of trial and error is required to know which ones are correct.

186670.overview: Manic Death Chase is a platform maze game where the screen scrolls left or right when you move your hero. You play the role of Pat who for reasons unknown is trapped in an underground cavern and has to attempt to escape. As you move along the platforms, you will encounter giant spiders or spikes and if you touch any then you lose one of three lives. There are also dead-ends but you are able to move back on yourself and jump to higher platforms.

186671.overview:
The Blibbles home planet is over-populated and so thousands need moving to another planet by cargo ship and as the Captain of the ship, it is your job to get them to their new home safely. Problem is, someone left their holding cell open and now the creatures are moving around the ship causing trouble. To make matters worse they are entering the engine room moving to a cargo transporter which is sending them to oblivion. You must use your scanner to move a Coerco-Stasis-Grille in their paths and transport them back to safety while avoiding rogue droids and a Wafoid.

Mayhem is a single screen game viewed from the side full of platforms and lifts which the Blibbles will move around before eventually reaching the transporter. You must move a sight and pick up the Grille and place it in the path of each emerging Blibble in the bottom right corner. You can move the sight around but before a Blibble touches the Grille you must hold down the fire button to transport it to safety. As you transport Blibbles, Droids will start appearing and these can be shot with your sight because if they touch the Grille it will move back to the top left of the screen and has to be picked up and placed again. A Wafoid also appears and moves diagonally and can't be destroyed so your sight and Grille need to avoid it. Once ten Blibbles reach the transporter, then it is game over.

186672.overview:
Your task is to destroy all Megabolts who have invaded your world over 64 screens on a 8x8 grid connected by various passages. The game is a maze game viewed from above with each maze shown on the whole screen and you must control a craft killing all the Megabolt's ships that move about the maze. To kill them you can either shoot them with your laser or you can crush them with part of a wall which you fire at to move. There is also a spinning yellow craft that moves about the maze and this can't be shot just avoided. Touch this spinning craft or a Megabolt and you lose one of six lives.

As you move about the maze you have a fuel gauge which is slowly decreasing and when this runs out you lose a live but you can collect moving orange diamonds to increase it. As well as the main playing area you can also see your score, lives, high score, how many Megabolts to destroy in that maze, your grid location and an alert which tells you which grids still have Megabolts active.

186673.overview:
Molecule Man is trapped inside a radioactive maze of 256 screens, and it's your job to get him out. To do this you must collect 16 circuits which are located at extreme points of the levels. You must regularly consume radiation tablets to fend off certain poisoning, and your initial supply of 20 is totally inadequate.

Fortunately, there are coins dotted around the levels, as well as ant-radiation tablet vending machines at which you can buy them. Coins can also be used to buy more time, or to blow up obstacles which make some sections difficult or impossible to access.

Viewed isometrically, the screen designs are intentionally surreal, each taking on an unlikely distorted real-world theme. If you find the initial level layouts too easy, too hard or too dull, you can design a new set with the bundled maze editor.

186674.overview: Based on the original television series that ran from 1978 to 1980, the player controls Monkey as he makes his way through four levels and rescue the princess from the evil dragon. In the first level, the player rides a cloud, and must use lightning bolts to destroy three waves of flying creatures. Finally, in the last level, the player must defeat the dragon by throwing spears at it, while avoiding its fire.

186676.overview:
Moon Buggy is a clone of the classic Atari game Moon Patrol. The player is the moon base commander, out on patrol in the ATMB (All Terrain Moon Buggy). An alien attack has penetrated the base's outer defences and its the player's job to see that this incursion is stopped.

The game features flying saucers that drop bombs, craters that must be jumped, boulders that must be blasted, incoming missiles, tanks and land mines. The buggy tracks left to right across the screen, it can accelerate, decelerate, fire missiles and jump but it cannot go backwards. Points are scored for enemies destroyed and distance travelled. The game records the top five scores for the gaming session.

202329.overview:
A once prosperous land inhabited by an evil wizard has stayed uninhabited long after he left. There are tales though that he left behind in his lair a golden statue which is priceless. You play as an adventurer who has entered the land looking for the buried treasure. The game is a flick-screen arcade adventure viewed from the side with elements of a platform game. There are eight skill levels to choose from and when the game is completed you start again on a higher skill level.

As you explore you will encounter buildings to explore as well as creatures and objects that will harm you. As you move about, you have a strength gauge which is slowly decreasing but you can find potions and food to keep it topped up. Touching creatures like bats or items like falling apples and water will decrease the gauge further and be wary of certain potions that are poison and an antidote needs to be found before you die and it's game over.

To succeed in your quest, certain items need to be found before you can get to the statue which are seven talismans scattered all over the surrounding area, two keys to unlock doors to enter buildings, and a candle to see in the underground section. A joystick or keyboard can be used to control your hero.

205606.overview:
Mission Mars is a side view vertical scrolling game where the screen scrolls constantly, and your mission is to navigate various caverns, each with five stages to raid them. As you fall downwards you must avoid or bomb various obstacles while making sure you don't touch the sides of the caverns. You are able to move left or right, downwards a short distance and back upwards.If you touch the sides of the caverns or any object then you lose one of five lives.

This was a conversion of the 1983 VIC-20 game Cavern Raider with a name change.

205609.overview: After all the Berks were destroyed in Berks, the creator Major Blink has decided to become a painter to make a living. You control Major Blink over various single screens full of different size blocks and paint them. To paint a block you have to paint all the sides which will complete the whole block but there are Teddies moving around the screen removing your work. Also moving around are Drones, sent by your previous employers who weren't happy at your failure but you do have a double laser to help. The Teddies can be destroyed but the Drones can only be stunned and if you touch the Teddies or Drones then you lose one of five lives. If you stand at the top of the screen in the red zone, no more Teddies will appear and once all the blocks are painted then you move to the next screen. There are five skill levels to choose from and they are Duffer, Novice, Normal, Expert and Master.

214569.overview: Manic Miner is a platform video game originally written for the ZX Spectrum by Matthew Smith and released by Bug-Byte in 1983 (later re-released by Software Projects). It is the first game in the Miner Willy series and among the early titles in the platform game genre. The game itself was inspired by the Atari 800 game Miner 2049er. It has since been ported to numerous home computers and video game consoles.

214571.overview: The ancient game of chess is recreated here, with all the traditional rules and game concepts. The game is in 2D, as the programmers felt this was the most effective use of available memory. Controls involve moving a pointer over the square to move a piece from, pressing space, then moving to the destination square and pressing space again. You can set the amount of time players (human and computer) have to plan moves, although an over-ride option to force a move instantly also exists. You can save and reload games, and at any point can move pieces either from current settings or from scratch, to completely customise the game or play out classic positions.

446241.overview: Munch-It is based on the arcade game Pac-Man where you have to move around a top view single screen maze and eat all the dots. While your eating the dots, there are three ghosts moving around the maze looking to kill you. If you touch a ghost then you lose one of three lives. In the four corners of the maze are power-pills and when eaten allow you to chase and eat the ghosts for a short time. Before the game starts you can select a skill level (1-4).

446321.overview: Mount Vesuvius is erupting and the sheherds and farmers that live in the houses beside the slopes need rescuing. You have been chosen to take your helicopter in this side view horizontal scrolling game where the screen scrolls when you move, and fly to all the houses and rescue as many people as you can. You start beside a cable car station and as you take off and fly you look for houses on the ground and land besides them to increase your passenger counter. You can only carry five people so once full you fly back to the station to drop them off and also re-fuel because as you fly your fuel decreases and when it is empty it is game over. You are required to pick up a minimum amount of people to carry on with the game and there is a set number of inhabitants that need rescuing to complete the game.

446322.overview:
Matrix and Laserzone is a double games pack containing the following two C16 conversions of Jeff Minter games:

Matrix
Laserzone

446331.overview: You stand outside a mansion which some say is haunted while others say it is cursed, and your quest is to enter and explore the mansion looking for a fabled diamond. The screen has text which describes each location you're in and you type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your surroundings.

446332.overview: Inspired by the arcade game Asteroids, Meteorites is a top view single screen shooter where you start in the middle of the screen blasting meteors moving in various directions around the screen. You turn in a 360 degree direction and using thrust moves you forward a short distance. When you hit a meteor it splits into smaller pieces and when these pieces are shot they disappear. If you are hit by a meteor then you lose one of three lives.

446347.overview:
Mindbenders is a collection of eight games to get the brain-cells working with puzzle, strategy and action games:

Repeat After Me: A memory game where you have to match the sequence the computer shows you by pressing buttons. You start with just one button pressed and if correct the computer then presses the same button and then another one. Every time you get the sequence correct the computer adds another button until you get the sequence wrong.

Jeff's Panel: You are presented with an 8 x 8 grid full of four different coloured squares in a formation. You let the computer know how many times to scramble the formation before you then have to put the squares back in their correct order. You are only allowed to slide a whole row or column to move any square.

Rotation: You are presented with a 4 x 4 grid with each square having a letter inside. You must move the letters around to put the them in order. When you select a letter to move it will rotate with four other letters in a clockwise direction. You cannot select a letter on the edge of the grid and you have one special move where you can swap two letters

Blackjack: A casino card game where you have to beat the dealer to win money by getting 21 or as close to without going over. You have two cards and you must decide whether to keep them or to receive another card. Once you are happy with your total or you go over 21 (Bust) the dealer plays. Two players can play the computer and both start with $1000 and you have the choice of how many decks to play with (1-6).

Labyrinth: A 1st person perspective game where you have to get to an exit in a 3D maze. You first can select the size of the maze before seeing a map of the maze. As you wander the maze, you can select the map but the aim is to escape without using the map.

Letter Slider: You are presented with a 3 x 3 grid full of squares with letters inside and one blank square. You must move the letters around the grid to put them in order using the blank square to put a letter in.

Magic Square: You are presented with a 3 x 3 grid with squares with a number inside and you have to highlight all the squares leaving square 5 in the middle blank. Pressing a number highlights certain squares and you keep pressing numbers to highlight the squares.

Word Search: You input up to 20 words before trying to find the words in a 20 x 20 grid full of letters. The words can be horizontal, vertical, diagonal and backwards.

446391.overview: Mail Trail is a top view single screen game where you have to deliver mail to a house within 28 days avoiding various obstacles and vehicles. Starting on the left of the screen you must reach a chosen house in an fenced off estate on the right of the screen. You first must move around trees before attempting to cross two railway tracks with speeding trains moving up and down the screen. Once past the railway lines, you have to cross two rivers by jumping on moving boats to get to the other side. You are now outside the estate with one entrance and inside is the house (coloured purple) but there are vehicles driving around the streets.

446392.overview:
Maniax is a Qix variant. The basic playing principle: the player controls a dot which can draw lines on the screen and when a closed figure is drawn, the colour of the area changes. Additionally there are enemies, either confined to the uncoloured or coloured areas, which cause the player sprite to die if touched. The goal is to colour 75% of the screen.

This variant reveals background images taken from 16 cities instead of just changing the screen colour. There are also various extras to pick up which give advantages like extra lives, frozen enemies or extra points. Triangles show negative effects when picked up, e.g. instant death or deceleration.

446395.overview: Megazap is a side view single screen shooter where you control a spacecraft, moving left or right, at the bottom of the screen blasting various aliens and meteors above over various levels. Each level has a set type of alien or meteor and these move in various waves like moving across the screen in formation, breaking from formation or just falling down the screen. The aliens will drop bombs and if you hit an alien, bomb or meteor then you lose one of three lives.

446417.overview:
Mercenary: The Second City is an expansion pack for Mercenary, which features the same gameplay and controls.

Following the successes over Targ's Central City, the controller of the BENSON computer relaxes and enjoys himself. Soon however, he grows bored and starts looking around for new challenges on the still hazardous Planet Targ. Rumors about the Palyar Commander's brother-in-law living in the southern hemisphere suggest that this may be a good challenge. In this Second City, the battle between Palyars and Mechanoids still rages... and nothing is as it seems.

446437.overview:
Mushroom Mania is a shoot 'em up that clones the Centipede game style.

The player must shoot at a giant centipede that moves down the playing field and can win additional points for shooting the mushrooms. The player must have care with the spiders, and with an indestructible enemy, the "hungry Pacperson".

446984.overview:
Math Games and Word Problems is an educational math compilation released as part of the "Public Domain Series" from Commodore Business Machines for the Plus/4 and C16.

Despite it being called the "Public Domain Series" the programs were NOT public domain/free.

This pack includes the following games/programs:

-   Tic Tac Arithmetic
-   Story Problems
-   Add and Subtract
-   Cash Register
-   Math Mania
-   Reverse
-   Number-Toe
-   Car Race Multiplication

The compilation pack was only officially released in the US and Canada, however all the games are compatible on both NTSC and PAL machines due to all the games being coded in BASIC.
